reflection.text:
Unblinded as cytochalasin B, an actin disruptor, my Microtubule stabilizers call (p=0.62) was wrong. I was anchored by reproducibly huge tub_mean z-scores (+7.5 at 1 uM, +31.3 at 3 uM, +27.7 at 10 uM) and the microscopist's stabilizer suggestion of dense perinuclear tubulin bundles/rings with multinucleation, which I let outweigh the weak split atlas vote.

I misattributed bright condensed tubulin to stabilization rather than secondary collapse/condensation after the actin cytoskeleton failed, and the flat dose-response (rho=+0.32, p=0.68 for both tub_mean and multinucleation) should have warned it was not classic stabilizer behavior.

Acquisition choices locked in the error: sampling only 1, 3, and duplicate 10 uM wells emphasized late toxic, highly condensed fields with no low-dose actin blebbing/contractility window and no replicate at 1-3 uM. I also never ran the discriminating actin-vs-tubulin counter-test I proposed, and protocol NSC never voted stabilizer (2/4 Epithelial at similarities 0.36-0.61, plus Eg5 and Protein synthesis singletons).
what_was_right: Detected a strong reproducible cytoskeletal/cytokinesis-failure phenotype: reduced density, shrunken cells (cell_area z=-8.4), misshapen nuclei (nuc_solidity z=-27.9, nuc_form_factor z=-24.0) and multinucleation (frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+8.4).

what_was_wrong: Atttributed tub_mean brightening (+7.5 to +31.3 in e2, e3, e7) to direct microtubule stabilization instead of secondary tubulin condensation after primary actin-filament loss and cytokinesis failure.
Over-weighted the microscopist Microtubule stabilizers suggestion (e5) and under-weighted that actin texture z-scores were larger than tubulin z-scores in the same high-dose wells (e3, e8).

## Unblinding

Compound: **cytochalasin B** (PubChem CID [5311281](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5311281))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Actin disruptors**.

## Reflection

Unblinded as cytochalasin B, an actin disruptor, my Microtubule stabilizers call (p=0.62) was wrong. I was anchored by reproducibly huge tub_mean z-scores (+7.5 at 1 uM, +31.3 at 3 uM, +27.7 at 10 uM) and the microscopist's stabilizer suggestion of dense perinuclear tubulin bundles/rings with multinucleation, which I let outweigh the weak split atlas vote.

In hindsight the actin channel held the true signal and was even stronger: act_glcm_contrast z=+36.0 to +56.2 and act_mean z=+27.6 exceeded tubulin, with cell_area z=-8.4, nuc_solidity z=-27.9 and frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+8.4 exactly fitting actin-dependent cytokinesis failure and cell shrinkage. I misattributed bright condensed tubulin to stabilization rather than secondary collapse/condensation after the actin cytoskeleton failed, and the flat dose-response (rho=+0.32, p=0.68 for both tub_mean and multinucleation) should have warned it was not classic stabilizer behavior.

Acquisition choices locked in the error: sampling only 1, 3, and duplicate 10 uM wells emphasized late toxic, highly condensed fields with no low-dose actin blebbing/contractility window and no replicate at 1-3 uM. I also never ran the discriminating actin-vs-tubulin counter-test I proposed, and protocol NSC never voted stabilizer (2/4 Epithelial at similarities 0.36-0.61, plus Eg5 and Protein synthesis singletons).

What was right:
- Detected a strong reproducible cytoskeletal/cytokinesis-failure phenotype: reduced density, shrunken cells (cell_area z=-8.4), misshapen nuclei (nuc_solidity z=-27.9, nuc_form_factor z=-24.0) and multinucleation (frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+8.4).
- Detected massive actin disruption alongside tubulin change (act_glcm_contrast z=+36.0 to +56.2, act_mean z=+27.6, act_std z=+19.0, tub_std z=+23.0) across e3, e7 and e8.
- Recognized atlas support was weak and split with no coherent consensus (e4: Eg5 1/2; e9: Epithelial 2/4 at similarities 0.36-0.61; k-neighbours split Protein synthesis/Eg5).

What was wrong or missed:
- Atttributed tub_mean brightening (+7.5 to +31.3 in e2, e3, e7) to direct microtubule stabilization instead of secondary tubulin condensation after primary actin-filament loss and cytokinesis failure.
- Over-weighted the microscopist Microtubule stabilizers suggestion (e5) and under-weighted that actin texture z-scores were larger than tubulin z-scores in the same high-dose wells (e3, e8).
- Ignored the non-significant dose-response (e10, e11 rho=+0.32 p=0.68) and lack of any NSC stabilizer vote, and duplicated toxic 10 uM (e8) instead of acquiring low-dose or actin-specific follow-up to discriminate actin disruptors.

Proposed next experiment: F-actin phalloidin imaging dose-response versus latrunculin/cytochalasin B control plus cell-free tubulin polymerization assay and washout live-imaging for binucleate formation to test primary actin-filament block with secondary tubulin condensation.
